claims.text: Adding a small amount of Hf to a refractory high-entropy alloy can improve its high-temperature oxygen resistance relative to the untreated alloy.
An Hf addition of 1–3% is expected to provide the proposed oxidation benefit.
The intervention is applicable to both as-cast and wrought refractory high-entropy alloys.
Hf addition will cause a protective HfO2 surface layer to form.
The resulting HfO2 layer will be stable and protective at high temperature.
The HfO2 layer will reduce oxidation of the underlying alloy.
The proposed oxidation benefit should occur from 800°C to 1200°C in an oxidizing atmosphere.
Improved oxygen resistance should enhance the alloy's structural integrity and service life under extreme conditions.
Prior work reports that a small Hf addition can improve room-temperature mechanical properties in a single-phase FCC high-entropy alloy through intermetallic precipitation.
The cited prior evidence supports the proposed HfO2-based oxidation mechanism in refractory high-entropy alloys.
After 100 hours at 1000°C in an oxidizing atmosphere, the Hf-modified alloy should exhibit better oxidation resistance and post-exposure mechanical properties than the unmodified control.
